summary: Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Gelden, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1972). He served at the University of Virginia from 1973 to 2024.

Jeffrey J. Kripal is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College (~1984–1989) and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1988–1993). In ~2002, he held a professorship at Rice University.
Jeffrey K. Riegel is a scholar in sinology. He held a post as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley (~1982–2007) and served at the University of Sydney (~2007–2017).

Jeffrey Kotyk works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied under Terry Russell and James A. Benn, earning an MA from Komazawa University (2015–2016) and a PhD from Leiden University (-2017). He held posts at Bologna and McMaster.

Jeffrey L. Broughton is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD from Columbia University (~1970–1975) and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (~1979).

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar in philosophy. He held academic posts at Cornell University (~1969–1974), Johns Hopkins University (~1974–1983), and Boston University (~1983–2020), as well as positions at UC Berkeley, Harvard, and Washington University in St. Louis.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Harvard University (~1964–1970). He held posts at the University of Toronto (~1969–1980), UC Berkeley (~1977–1980), and the University of Michigan.
Jeffrey S. Lidke works in religious studies and Indology. He has held posts at Berry College and at the University of Virginia, where he was visiting assistant professor of religion (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under W. S. Karunatillake and Karen C. Lang, completing his PhD at the University of Virginia, and became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (~1968–1972), Princeton University (~1972–1977), and the California Culinary Academy. He served as a professor at Princeton University from ~1987 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen, William M. Bodiford, and James L. Fitzgerald. He has taught at UCLA and UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006). He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Gudrun Bühnemann, Charles Hallisey, and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held professorships at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (~2001) and at the University of Oslo (2003).

Jens Schlieter is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Bonn (~1987–1997) and became a professor at the University of Bern in ~2006.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Munich, Göttingen, and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held professorships at Göttingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, Free University of Berlin, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (-2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Oregon (~1962–1966) and Stanford University (~1968–1974), and held an academic post at Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a Polish linguist. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961) and subsequently spent his career there (~1961–2012), serving as Professor from ~1980 to 2010.

Jessie Pons is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University (-2011) and was Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).
Ji Hao is a sinologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Rouzer at the University of Minnesota, where he completed a PhD. He held a post at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).
